religions.name: hinduism
religions.began: no single founder; roots in the vedas, c. 1500 bce, and older
religions.followers: about 1.2 billion, mostly in india and nepal
religions.founder: none; the vedas were "heard" by ancient seers, the rishis
religions.scriptures: the vedas and upanishads; the epics, the mahabharata (with the bhagavad gita) and the ramayana; the puranas
religions.places: varanasi on the ganges, and thousands of temples and pilgrimage sites
religions.summary: the family of traditions of india, called by many followers sanatana dharma, "the eternal way". it includes many gods seen as forms of one reality, and belief in karma, rebirth, and liberation.
religions.creation: the universe is created, sustained, and dissolved again and again, without beginning. in one telling, brahma the creator is born on a lotus from the navel of vishnu. an old hymn of the rigveda asks who really knows how it began.
religions.age: time runs in vast cycles. one day of brahma, a kalpa, lasts 4.32 billion years, close to the scientific age of the earth. we now live in the kali yuga, the last and darkest of four ages, which tradition says began in 3102 bce.
religions.story: no beginning and no end in hindu tradition, the universe was not made once. it is created, kept, and dissolved again and again, in cycles without beginning or end. in one telling, vishnu sleeps on the great serpent shesha, floating on the cosmic ocean. a lotus grows from his navel, and on it brahma is born, who creates the worlds. in time shiva dissolves them, and the cycle begins again. these three gods are the trimurti . the oldest scripture, the rigveda, has a more puzzled hymn of creation. it says that in the beginning there was "neither being nor non-being", and ends by asking who truly knows how it all began: "perhaps even the one who watches from the highest heaven does not know." the ages of the world time is measured on a vast scale. a cycle of four yugas , or ages, lasts 4,320,000 years: age how long what it is like satya yuga 1,728,000 years the age of truth: dharma stands on four legs treta yuga 1,296,000 years dharma on three legs; the age of rama dvapara yuga 864,000 years dharma on two legs; the age of krishna kali yuga 432,000 years dharma on one leg; the age of strife, which is now a thousand such cycles make one day of brahma, a kalpa of 4.32 billion years, and his night lasts as long. this is strikingly close to the scientific age of the earth, 4.54 billion years, though the tradition means something different: a rhythm, not a single beginning. by tradition, the kali yuga began in 3102 bce, when krishna left the world. at its end, kalki, the last avatar of vishnu, will come to begin a new age of truth. the great stories two epics carry much of hindu tradition. the ramayana, told by the sage valmiki , follows prince rama of ayodhya, an avatar of vishnu, whose wife sita is carried off by the demon king ravana. with the help of hanuman and an army of monkeys, rama rescues her. the mahabharata, said to be told by vyasa , is the story of a great war between two branches of one family. on the battlefield, the warrior arjuna loses heart, and his charioteer, krishna , teaches him the bhagavad gita , about doing one's duty without selfishness and about love for god. what historians can show hinduism has no single founder or starting date. its oldest texts, the vedas , were composed in early sanskrit from about 1500 bce and passed down by memory with extraordinary accuracy. they may draw on older traditions of the indus civilization and of india's many peoples. the upanishads , from about 800 bce, turned to the nature of the self, atman , and ultimate reality, brahman . the epics took their final form between about 400 bce and 400 ce, and the gupta age saw the first stone temples and the puranas, books of stories about the gods. paths of devotion and knowledge from about 600 ce, tamil poet-saints sang of bhakti , passionate personal devotion, and it spread across india. philosophers argued about how the self and god are related: adi shankara taught that they are one, and ramanuja that the soul is saved by loving god. later saints like chaitanya , mirabai , and tulsidas wrote and sang in the everyday languages of the people. hindu kings built temples as far away as cambodia, where angkor wat was dedicated to vishnu. the modern age under british rule, reformers like ram mohan roy worked to change practices they saw as wrong, and ramakrishna taught that all religions lead to god. his follower swami vivekananda brought hindu teaching to the west in 1893. mahatma gandhi drew on the gita in the struggle for independence. today about 1.2 billion people are hindu, and yoga , meditation, and ideas like karma are known around the world. belief and practice one ultimate reality, brahman, worshipped in many forms: vishnu, shiva, the goddess, and many more. samsara , the cycle of rebirth, driven by karma, and moksha , liberation from it. dharma: living rightly according to one's duties. puja at home and in temples, the sacred sound om , pilgrimage, and festivals like diwali . see also part 4 and part 5 of the main history.

events.text: "then there was neither being nor non-being." the creation hymn of the rigveda asks how it all began, and ends: perhaps even the one who watches from the highest heaven does not know
vishnu sleeps on the great serpent shesha, floating on the cosmic ocean. a lotus grows from his navel, and on it brahma is born and creates the worlds

a day of brahma, a kalpa, lasts 4.32 billion years, and his night as long. at night the worlds dissolve; at dawn they are made again. after a hundred years of such days, all dissolves and a new brahma is born
vishnu, as the fish matsya, warns manu of a great flood and tows his boat to safety with the seeds of all life and the seven sages
the age of truth. dharma stands firm on four legs; people are good, wise, and live very long lives
dharma stands on three legs. rama, the seventh avatar of vishnu, rescues his wife sita from the demon king ravana: the story of the ramayana
dharma stands on two legs. krishna, the eighth avatar, is born; he guides arjuna in the great war at kurukshetra, and his teaching becomes the bhagavad gita
krishna leaves the world and the kali yuga begins: the age of strife, 432,000 years long, in which we live now
the indus cities flourish; some of their seals show figures in yoga-like poses, but how they relate to later hinduism is debated
the hymns of the rigveda are composed in early sanskrit and passed down by memory, word for word, for many centuries
the upanishads explore the self (atman), ultimate reality (brahman), karma, and rebirth
the great epics, the mahabharata and the ramayana, take their final form; the bhagavad gita becomes part of the mahabharata
in the gupta age, the puranas are written, and the first stone temples to vishnu, shiva, and the goddess are built
tamil poet-saints, the alvars and nayanars, sing of loving devotion (bhakti) to vishnu and shiva
adi shankara teaches that the self and brahman are one (advaita), and founds monasteries at the four corners of india
ramanuja teaches that loving devotion to vishnu leads to liberation
the khmer king suryavarman ii builds angkor wat in cambodia, a vast temple to vishnu
chaitanya leads ecstatic singing of krishna's names in bengal; in rajasthan, mirabai writes songs of love for krishna
tulsidas begins the ramcharitmanas, a retelling of the ramayana in hindi, still recited across north india
ram mohan roy founds the brahmo samaj, calling for reform and the worship of one god
swami vivekananda speaks at the parliament of the world's religions in chicago, bringing hindu teaching to the west
india becomes independent as a secular republic; partition divides hindus and muslims with great bloodshed
a. c. bhaktivedanta swami prabhupada founds the hare krishna movement in new york
about 1.2 billion hindus live mainly in india and nepal; the kumbh mela, held every twelve years at prayagraj, is often called the largest gathering of people on earth

religions.name: buddhism
religions.followers: about 500 million, mostly in east and southeast asia
religions.founder: siddhartha gautama, the buddha, "the awakened one"
religions.scriptures: the pali canon (tipitaka); many mahayana sutras; the tibetan canon
religions.places: lumbini, bodh gaya, sarnath, and kushinagar, the places of the buddha's life
religions.summary: the path taught by the buddha to end suffering, through understanding its causes, living ethically, and training the mind. it does not depend on a creator god.
religions.creation: the buddha set aside the question of how the world began as not helpful for ending suffering. buddhist texts describe countless world systems that form, last, decay, and form again.
religions.age: time has no known beginning. it is measured in kalpas, eons so long that a mountain wiped with a silk cloth once a century would wear away first. many buddhas have come in past eons, and one, maitreya, is still to come.
religions.story: the question the buddha set aside a monk once demanded that the buddha tell him whether the world had a beginning, and whether it would end. the buddha answered with a story. a man is shot with a poisoned arrow, but refuses to let the doctor pull it out until he knows who shot it, what the bow was made of, and what feathers were on the arrow. he will die before he finds out. in the same way, the buddha said, questions about the beginning of the world do not help to end suffering, which is what matters. still, buddhist texts describe a universe of immense size and age. there are countless world systems, each passing through long ages of forming, lasting, falling apart, and emptiness, and then forming again. time is measured in kalpas , eons so long that, it is said, a mountain of solid rock wiped with a silk cloth once every hundred years would be worn away before a kalpa ended. no first beginning can be found. the long road to awakening according to tradition, countless eons ago an ascetic named sumedha met the buddha dipankara and vowed to become a buddha himself. over hundreds of lives, as an animal, a king, a merchant, and a beggar, he perfected generosity, patience, and wisdom. these lives are told in the jataka tales. in his last life he was born as prince siddhartha. the life of the buddha siddhartha gautama was born in the lumbini garden to queen maya and king suddhodana of the shakya people. his father, wanting him to be a great king, kept him inside the palace, and he married yasodhara . at 29 he went out and saw an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering holy man. shaken, he left his home to search for an end to suffering. for six years he tried extreme fasting, until he was almost dead. then he chose a middle way. sitting under a tree at bodh gaya, he was attacked by mara, the tempter, but touched the earth as his witness, and in the night he awoke to the truth. he taught for 45 years, founding the sangha of monks and, at the urging of mahapajapati , of nuns. his attendant ananda remembered his words. at 80 he passed into final nirvana . what historians can show most historians accept that the buddha was a real teacher who lived in northern india, dying around 400 bce, though the tradition dates his life earlier. his teachings were passed down by memory and written in the pali language in sri lanka in the first century bce, the oldest complete buddhist scripture. the emperor ashoka left inscriptions from the 200s bce that show buddhism already honored and spreading. the teaching the buddha's first sermon set out the four noble truths : life involves dukkha , suffering; suffering comes from craving; it can end; and the way to end it is the eightfold path . he taught karma and rebirth, but also anatta : there is no fixed self that passes from life to life. the goal is nirvana, the blowing out of craving, and the path is ethics, meditation , and wisdom. buddhists "take refuge" in the buddha, the dharma , and the sangha. across asia buddhism spread along trade routes. theravada , "the way of the elders", went to sri lanka and southeast asia. mahayana , with its ideal of the bodhisattva and new sutras , went to china, korea, and japan, where philosophers like nagarjuna were studied and bodhidharma was remembered as the founder of zen . pilgrims like xuanzang walked to india for texts. vajrayana took root in tibet with padmasambhava and saints like milarepa . in japan, dogen and nichiren founded new schools. in india itself, buddhism faded after the destruction of nalanda around 1193. the modern age in 1956, b. r. ambedkar led half a million dalits into buddhism as a protest against caste. in 1959 the dalai lama , tenzin gyatso , fled tibet. teachers like thich nhat hanh brought meditation to the west. today about 500 million people are buddhist, and the tradition expects that one day, when the teaching is forgotten, a new buddha, maitreya , will come. belief and practice the four noble truths and the eightfold path. karma, rebirth, not-self, and the goal of nirvana. meditation, chanting, and offerings at a stupa or temple. the three refuges: the buddha, the dharma, and the sangha. see also part 5 of the main history, and the middle ages for buddhism in china, japan, and southeast asia.

events.text: the buddha teaches that no first beginning of the round of rebirth can be found. world systems without number arise, last, decline, and pass away
each world passes through four long stages: forming, lasting, falling apart, and emptiness, and then forms again
the ascetic sumedha meets the buddha dipankara and vows to become a buddha himself. over countless lives he perfects generosity, patience, and wisdom, as told in the jataka tales
the future buddha waits in heaven for the right time, then chooses to be born as prince siddhartha
queen maya gives birth to siddhartha in the lumbini garden. the baby takes seven steps, and a sage foretells he will be either a great king or a buddha
most historians place the buddha's birth around 480 bce at lumbini, in modern nepal; the theravada tradition dates it to 623 bce
outside the palace, siddhartha sees an old man, a sick man, a corpse, and a wandering holy man. he leaves his family and his wealth to seek the end of suffering
sitting under the bodhi tree at bodh gaya, he overcomes the tempter mara and wakes up to the truth: he is now the buddha
in the deer park at sarnath, the buddha teaches the four noble truths to five companions, who become the first monks
after 45 years of teaching, the buddha passes into final nirvana at kushinagar
according to tradition, 500 monks meet to recite the teachings together; they are passed down by memory for centuries
the emperor ashoka turns to buddhism after the slaughter at kalinga and sends teachers across and beyond india, including his son mahinda to sri lanka
monks in sri lanka write down the teachings in the pali language, the pali canon of theravada buddhism
buddhism reaches china along the silk roads; by tradition the white horse temple is founded at luoyang
mahayana sutras, such as the lotus sutra and the perfection of wisdom, appear, teaching the path of the bodhisattva
nagarjuna teaches that all things are empty of fixed, separate existence
buddhism reaches korea
the monastery university of nalanda is founded in india; it will draw students from all over asia
a korean king sends an image of the buddha and sutras to japan
the chinese monk xuanzang walks to india to collect scriptures and brings back hundreds of texts
samye, the first buddhist monastery in tibet, is completed
the great stupa of borobudur is built on java
the diamond sutra is printed in china, the oldest dated printed book
invaders destroy nalanda; buddhism fades away in most of india
dogen returns from china and brings soto zen to japan
the fifth dalai lama becomes the ruler of tibet
b. r. ambedkar and about half a million dalits become buddhists at nagpur, rejecting caste
the fourteenth dalai lama flees chinese rule in tibet and settles in india
about 500 million buddhists live mostly in east and southeast asia; buddhist meditation has spread worldwide
when the teaching has been forgotten, maitreya, the next buddha, will be born and teach the path again

religions.name: sikhism
religions.followers: about 25 to 30 million, most in the punjab
religions.founder: guru nanak, followed by nine more human gurus
religions.scriptures: the guru granth sahib, treated as the living guru
religions.places: the harmandir sahib (golden temple) in amritsar, and the five takhts
religions.summary: devotion to the one creator, remembered through god's name, honest work, and sharing with others. it teaches that all people are equal, and it was shaped by ten gurus over two centuries.
religions.creation: before creation there was only the one, formless and in deep stillness. by god's will, the hukam, the universe came to be, with countless worlds and skies.
religions.age: guru nanak taught that only the creator knows when the world was made: no scholar, holy book, or calendar can say. many sikhs see science and scripture as describing the same vast creation.
religions.story: the one, before all things the guru granth sahib begins with ik onkar , "there is one god". god is the creator, the truth, without fear, without hate, beyond time, never born and self-existent. before creation, in the words of guru nanak , "for endless ages there was only darkness": no earth or sky, no day or night, no sun or moon, only the one in deep, formless stillness. by the hukam , god's will, the universe came into being. "with one word you made the vast expanse," guru nanak sang, "and hundreds of thousands of rivers began to flow." there are worlds beneath worlds, and hundreds of thousands of skies above; people have grown tired of searching for their limits. and when was the world made? guru nanak asked the question himself: "what was that time, what was that moment, what day, what date ... when the world was made?" the scholars do not know, nor the writers of holy books, nor the yogis. "the creator who made the world knows alone." many sikhs see the vast universe described by science as a sign of the same greatness. the first guru guru nanak was born in 1469 in the punjab, then ruled by muslim sultans, into a hindu family. as a young man he worked as a storekeeper and spent his free time in prayer with his muslim friend and musician, bhai mardana . according to tradition, one morning he went into the river bein to bathe and disappeared for three days. when he came back, he said: "there is no hindu, there is no muslim", meaning that god sees people, not labels. with mardana he made long journeys to teach, and his hymns were sung to music, as kirtan still is. in about 1521 he settled at kartarpur, where his followers lived as farmers, prayed together, and ate together. he taught three simple duties: remember god's name ( naam simran ), earn an honest living, and share with others. ten gurus before he died in 1539, guru nanak passed his light to a disciple, guru angad , who spread the gurmukhi script, while his wife mata khivi ran the langar . guru amar das insisted that everyone eat together, rich or poor, before they could see him, and guru ram das founded amritsar. guru arjan gathered the hymns of the gurus, and of hindu and muslim saints, into one book and built the harmandir sahib with doors on all four sides, open to all. in 1606 the mughal emperor had him put to death. after that, guru hargobind wore two swords, for spiritual and worldly power, miri piri . guru tegh bahadur was executed in 1675 for standing up for the right of hindus to practice their faith. in 1699 guru gobind singh , the tenth guru, called the sikhs together at vaisakhi and founded the khalsa , initiating the panj pyare with amrit and giving them the five ks . before his death in 1708 he declared that there would be no more human gurus: the scripture itself would be the guru forever. what historians can show unlike older faiths, sikhism began in well-recorded times, and the basic story of the ten gurus is not in doubt. the stories of guru nanak's life, the janamsakhis, were written down decades after his death and include miracles; historians treat the details with care, but his hymns survive in the scripture in his own words. empire and partition after the gurus, sikhs fought mughal and afghan armies. banda singh bahadur led an uprising, and later ranjit singh built a sikh empire in the punjab and covered the harmandir sahib in gold, making it the golden temple. the british conquered the punjab in 1849, and in 1919 their troops massacred hundreds at amritsar. partition in 1947 split the punjab in two, and in 1984 the indian army stormed the golden temple, followed by the killing of thousands of sikhs. today about 25 to 30 million sikhs live around the world. belief and practice one god, waheguru , who is in everything and everyone. all people are equal, whatever their caste, sex, or religion. worship in the gurdwara with the sangat , and seva , selfless service. the langar, a free meal for anyone who comes. the goal: to live free of ego and to merge with god, like a drop of water in the ocean. see also part 7 of the main history.

events.text: "for endless ages there was only darkness." there was no earth and no sky, no day or night, no sun or moon: only the one, in deep, formless stillness
by the hukam, the will of the one, the universe comes into being: "with one word you made the vast expanse, and hundreds of thousands of rivers began to flow"
guru nanak sings of worlds beneath worlds and hundreds of thousands of skies above, too many to count
"what was that time, what was that moment ... when the world was made?" no scholar or holy book knows; only the creator knows
nanak is born at talwandi, now nankana sahib in pakistan, into a hindu family
nanak goes into the river bein and disappears for three days. he returns saying "there is no hindu, there is no muslim", and begins his mission
guru nanak makes long journeys with the musician mardana, across india and, by tradition, to tibet, sri lanka, mecca, and baghdad
guru nanak settles at kartarpur, where his followers farm, pray, sing, and eat together
guru nanak dies, naming his disciple angad as the second guru; guru angad spreads the gurmukhi script
guru amar das insists that everyone, rich or poor, eat together in the langar before meeting him
guru ram das founds the city of amritsar around a sacred pool
guru arjan compiles the adi granth, the sikh scripture, and installs it in the harmandir sahib at amritsar
guru arjan is tortured and put to death on the orders of the mughal emperor jahangir, the first sikh martyr
guru hargobind wears two swords, for spiritual and worldly power, and builds the akal takht
guru tegh bahadur is beheaded in delhi on aurangzeb's orders after defending the right of hindus to keep their faith
at the vaisakhi festival, guru gobind singh founds the khalsa, the order of initiated sikhs, with the five beloved ones
before he dies, guru gobind singh declares that the scripture, the guru granth sahib, will be the guru forever
banda singh bahadur, who led a sikh uprising against mughal rule, is captured and executed in delhi
ranjit singh takes lahore and goes on to build the sikh empire
under ranjit singh the upper floors of the harmandir sahib are covered in gold, and it becomes known as the golden temple
after two wars, the british conquer the punjab
british troops fire on a crowd gathered in the jallianwala bagh at amritsar on vaisakhi day, killing hundreds
partition splits the punjab between india and pakistan; millions of sikhs leave their homes in the west
the indian army storms the golden temple; after indira gandhi is killed by her sikh bodyguards, thousands of sikhs are murdered in riots
about 25 to 30 million sikhs live mostly in the punjab, with large communities in britain, canada, and the united states
by remembering god's name and living truthfully, the soul is freed from ego and merges with the one, like a drop of water in the ocean

people.name: guru ram das

people.name: guru hargobind

glossary.definition: "nectar": the sweetened water used when a sikh is initiated into the khalsa.
the five signs worn by initiated sikhs: kesh (uncut hair), kara (steel bracelet), kanga (comb), kachera (cotton undershorts), and kirpan (small sword).
"the guru's door": a sikh place of worship, where the guru granth sahib is kept and the langar is served.
"from the guru's mouth": the script in which the punjabi language and the guru granth sahib are written.
"teacher": in sikhism, the ten human gurus from nanak to gobind singh, and after them the scripture itself.
the sikh scripture, with hymns by six gurus and by hindu and muslim saints, treated as the living guru.
the will or order of god, by which everything happens.
"there is one god": the first words of the guru granth sahib, and the symbol of sikhism.
the community of initiated sikhs, founded by guru gobind singh in 1699.
singing the hymns of the scripture to music, the heart of sikh worship.
the free kitchen in every gurdwara, where all sit together and eat the same food, whatever their caste or faith.
worldly and spiritual power, shown by guru hargobind's two swords.
remembering god by repeating and meditating on god's name.
"the five beloved ones": the first five sikhs initiated into the khalsa in 1699.
the congregation of sikhs gathered in worship.
selfless service to others, without thought of reward.
the spring harvest festival, on which the khalsa was founded in 1699.
"wonderful lord": the name sikhs most often use for god.
